_comment: Tags excluded from default PR Maestro batches. Zephyr tier labels: detox/maestro/README.md.
_ROOT_CAUSE_QUIC: SUPERSEDES the TLS story in _DIAGNOSIS_CORRECTION. Verified 2026-08-11 against three separate servers (CI w6eew3y1, local kxrxghk6, local nynohsqb) from iOS simulator device logs. The iOS connect/login flakes are HTTP/3 (QUIC) transport failures, NOT certificate trust failures. Evidence: (1) the servers advertise 'alt-svc: h3=":443"' and the app honours it — 1400-1600 h3stream lines per run; (2) a failed login POST to /api/v4/users/login was an h3 task that died with -1005 NSURLErrorNetworkConnectionLost, surfaced in-app as 'URLSessionTask failed with error: The network connection was lost'; the retry also ran over h3 and got 200, so the retry masks it rather than falling back to h2; (3) trust evaluation SUCCEEDS every time it completes ('TLS Trust result 0' = errSecSuccess); there is no rejected chain, untrusted root or hostname mismatch anywhere in the logs. The -1202/-1203 strings previously cited are CFBundle localized-message lookups, not errors. (4) CRITICALLY: all 11 'Cancelled during verify block' lines are immediately preceded by a CFNetwork 'summary for unused connection' — they are the losing side of normal h2/h3 connection racing being discarded, i.e. benign noise. That signature was never evidence of a defect, and several tags were excluded for years of runs on the strength of it. Consequence: 'intermittent TLS infra, not fixable app-side (OS trust evaluation)' is WRONG. The named mechanism is QUIC connection teardown on the iOS Simulator, which is potentially addressable app-side (HTTP/3 disable or fallback, ideally RUNNING_E2E-gated). That is a Product Engineering decision — tracked separately, not in this file.
_DIAGNOSIS_CORRECTION: STILL VALID (labelling): 'Assertion is false: id: tab_bar.home.tab is visible' failures were NOT login failures — wait_for_server_connect_complete.yml made the login-form wait optional and then asserted the home tab, so a failed SERVER CONNECT was reported with a login error message. #9971 fixed the mislabel by asserting notVisible:server_form.display_help first. SUPERSEDED (cause): this note previously concluded the underlying cause was TLS trust evaluation being cancelled against a valid Let's Encrypt chain. That conclusion is wrong — see _ROOT_CAUSE_QUIC. The dropped-keystroke cause it also documented is real and is now caught at input by the SEC-11051 set-and-verify in _enter_url_and_connect.yml.
_UNEXCLUDED_2026_08_11: MM-T1325, MM-T3260 (iOS only), MM-T5611, MM-T67856_1, MM-T67856_2 were un-excluded on 2026-08-11 after each was run locally on a freshly provisioned+seeded server (iOS 26.2, iPhone 17 Pro, RUNNING_E2E build). MM-T1325 clock_display: PASSED — it had never been probed, and was carried on the _DIAGNOSIS_CORRECTION TLS rationale it was never tested against; it reached the timezone screen through connect+login with no TLS involvement at all. MM-T3260 help_url: PASSED — was excluded on BOTH platforms, i.e. zero coverage anywhere; the browser hand-off opened and dismissed via the breadcrumb with the reopen recovery unused. MM-T67856_1/_2: PASSED locally, and previously PASSED on the CI probe run 31324371751. MM-T5611 was re-proven on iOS and fully un-excluded on 2026-08-29 (see _UNEXCLUDED_2026_08_29). Caveat: the QUIC flake in _ROOT_CAUSE_QUIC is real and unfixed, so these can still fail intermittently at connect/login. That is a transport defect with a named owner, not a reason to keep the flows dark. If a tag proves genuinely unstable in CI, re-exclude it WITH the failing run ID.
_UNEXCLUDED_2026_08_29: MM-T5603 and MM-T5611 were un-excluded from the ios list on 2026-08-29 after each flow passed 3x consecutively (clean server bookmark state between runs) on a iOS 26.3 iPhone 17 Pro simulator with a RUNNING_E2E CI build of fix/detox-hittest-wip-remaining, the test_bookmark.png fixture staged CI-style into the AppGroup FileProvider.LocalStorage 'File Provider Storage' dir (staging step now documented in the README local setup), and the test server config aligned with Matterwick CI. MM-T5603: the historical 'Error uploading file. Please try again.' failure NEVER reproduced (0 occurrences across all runs; upload POST and channel_bookmark.file.upload_complete succeeded in-flow every time) — the intermittent mechanism from 2026-08-11 remains unknown and unproven; if CI reproduces it, re-exclude WITH the failing run ID per the policy in _UNEXCLUDED_2026_08_11. MM-T5611: the iOS long-press via id regex channel_bookmark\.[a-z0-9]{26} resolved the bookmark Pressable and opened the options sheet on every run; non-vacuity was proven with two negative-control probes that both FAILED as required (long-press on a bogus channel_bookmark\.zzzz... id fails to resolve; long-press on the composer post input never surfaces channel_bookmark.options.edit), so the flow fails when the feature is broken. Do not regress to text: selectors for the bookmark row — see the full-string-regex trap in GUIDELINES.md Selectors. The *_picker.yml sub-flows stay structurally skipped in PR batches on both platforms; channel_bookmark_file_android_picker.yml was never a runtime path on iOS (the parent invokes it only under platform: Android).
_MM-T67856: RESOLVED 2026-08-30 — see _UNEXCLUDED_2026_08_30. Historical skip rationale: CI 32379773017 (PR #10081, 7a6c8d35c) attach_logs.yml failed in 78s with Maestro retry dump 'Assertion is false: false is true' (no element id). Same flow passed on 32366779289 and 32345857598. MM-T67856_1/_2 still run. Mechanism of that exact failure remains unknown — the tag is resolved by the stability bar, not by a diagnosing fix.
_UNEXCLUDED_2026_08_30: MM-T67856 was un-excluded from the ios list on 2026-08-30 after attach_logs.yml passed 5x consecutively inside the full PR iOS batch (7 flows, CI batch order, siblings included) against https://test-local-e2e.test.mattermost.cloud (server 11.11.0 — same train as CI), provisioned through the repo's own detox/provision tool plus the repo's fixtures/seed.ts per run. Run 1 was on the untouched fresh instance; runs 2-5 re-seeded fresh random-prefix teams/channels/users on the same server with a fresh app install and CI-style fixture staging each time. Per-batch JUnit captured for all 35 verdicts: 35/35 green, zero flakes. Non-vacuity was proven with a negative control: with SupportSettings.AllowDownloadLogs=false the flow FAILED exactly at 'No visible element found: id: app_logs_download_button' (exit 1); the flag was restored after. Two server-config findings are baked into the CI template by ea7530bf1 (re-apply the maestro server baseline per job): (1) the login username placeholder is assembled from server auth config — 'Email, Username or AD/LDAP Username' only appears when email + username + LDAP sign-in are all enabled, so a stock/off-LDAP server breaks login.yml via its full-string regex match; the baseline step provisions a label-only LDAP config ONLY when LDAP is disabled so real directories are never touched; (2) the T67856_4 AllowDownloadLogs flip was trap-protected only — the in-step EXIT trap does not fire on runner hard-kills or skip paths, so a crashed job could leave AllowDownloadLogs=false poisoning every later attach_logs run on that server; the template now restores in a standalone always()-conditioned step per platform. Caveat: the QUIC transport flake (_ROOT_CAUSE_QUIC) remains real and unfixed — intermittent connect/login failures stay possible; re-exclude WITH the failing run ID per the policy in _UNEXCLUDED_2026_08_11.
_DEAD_ENTRIES_REMOVED: MM-T1411, MM-T4832 and MM-T4833 were removed from the ios list on 2026-08-11. They were dead entries: run_ci_batches.sh already skips every detox/maestro/flows/calls/* flow on iOS unconditionally (CallKit/WebRTC do not work on the simulator), so the tag exclusions never fired. Removing them restores no coverage — it stops this file overstating what is tag-excluded. Getting calls running on an iOS simulator is a separate problem.
_MM-T3260_ANDROID: Skip Android ONLY: CI run 30331493720 (PR #9893, SHA 9f1496e) — help_url.yml failed with 'Unable to launch app com.mattermost.rnbeta' after ~136s; the Chrome Custom Tab hand-off leaves the driver unable to relaunch the app on API 35. This is a DIFFERENT cause from the iOS exclusion and has NOT been re-tested — the 2026-08-11 verification covered iOS only. Do not un-exclude on the strength of the iOS result.
